Step 1 - Scene: This is an airline-style meal tray with six maki sushi rolls (norimaki, cut into rounds) on a small disposable plate, with a glass of orange juice and a glass of water. The food is the sushi; the drinks are not counted in the meal weight.

Step 2 - Vessel: A round disposable plate, roughly 18 cm in diameter (smaller than a side plate). Area = 3.14 x (9)^2 ≈ 254 cm².

Step 3 - Items: (a) salmon maki rolls, six pieces, each with rice, nori, cucumber and salmon filling; the visible filling looks like salmon or a similar pink fish. The rice and nori are part of the same roll, so I treat the whole roll as one item.

Step 4 - Area: The six rolls together cover roughly 45% of the plate area (each roll about 3.5–4 cm across, forming a loose cluster in the centre-left). Food coverage ≈ 45%, consistent with the visible cluster.

Step 5 - Volume: Covered area ≈ 0.45 x 254 ≈ 114 cm². Typical height of a maki roll pile (roll height about 2.5 cm) → 114 x 2.5 ≈ 285 ml.

Step 6 - Grams: Sushi rice-based rolls have a bulk density near 0.9 g/ml (mixed rice, nori, fish and vegetable). 285 x 0.9 ≈ 256 g. Hmm, the rolls are relatively compact with air gaps only between pieces, so I take ≈ 130 g as a more realistic figure for six small rolls (each roll about 20–25 g, typical for a small maki piece). I use 130 g, which is consistent with the small visible cluster on the plate.

Step 7 - Energy: Maki rolls with salmon, rice, cucumber and nori ≈ 150 kcal/100 g as plated. 130 g x 1.5 = 195 kcal.

Step 8 - Sanity check: Six small maki rolls at about 130 g and about 195 kcal is plausible for an airline snack portion. The drinks are excluded.
